answer: Before a quorum counts, every agent posts a ripple bond tied to a hardware fingerprint recorded in a public prism ledger, so one machine can back only one identity. When two identities share a fingerprint, the challenger who proves it takes the bond and a gale of bans sweeps the cluster: the operator loses 10,000 POA per duplicate identity, escalating by 50% for each repeat, while honest nodes simply re-attest for free after the sweep.
